summary: Full-extraction pass over ten stored Malaysia MM2H documents: four parliamentary replies (2019-2021), the PAC media statement (2021) and follow-up report DR.5/2022, and four MOTAC documents (category table, May 2025 notice, system announcement, Silver category page). Adds approvals for 'other' nationalities and nationality counts, 5,396 applications returned during the freeze, 340 licensed agents, the value of homes bought by participants, and the non-money rules (stay, ages, pass terms, withdrawal limits, child age limits, participant cap) of the 2021 and 2024 regimes, plus three events.

observations.notes: All nationalities outside the top ten. The ten listed nationalities plus this row add up to the printed table total of 43,943; the reply's text gives 43,466 approvals for the same period (difference not explained).
Approved applications came from foreign nationals of 131 countries (base: approvals, 2002 to November 2018).
Approved applications 2011 to July 2019 came from nationals of 131 countries (base: approvals).

events.title: Immigration Department takes over MM2H from the Tourism Ministry
events.description: The Immigration Department (JIM, Home Ministry) took over the MM2H programme from MOTAC from 16 Sept 2021 and began recording fixed-deposit withdrawals for home purchase, health and education. (The Director-General says in the transcript the takeover was in August 2021.)
events.quote: JIM telah mengambil alih Program MM2H dari MOTAC bermula pada 16 September 2021.

events.title: Children up to 34 allowed as MM2H dependants
events.description: The Home Minister signed the Immigration (Amendment) Regulations 2022 on 14 March 2022; the amended Immigration Circular raises the age limit for child dependants to 34, if unmarried and not working in Malaysia (gazetted the day before the 16 March 2022 hearing, as stated orally).
events.quote: Yang Berhormat Menteri pada 14 Mac yang lalu telah menandatangani Peraturan-

events.title: Predecessor of MM2H began in 1996
events.description: The Home Ministry's secretary-general told the PAC that the programme that preceded MM2H started in 1996 and had never been fully reviewed in more than 20 years (oral statement).
events.quote: Ini kerana program yang ada sebelum ini bermula pada tahun 1996 lagi.

events.title: MM2H notice: SEZ homes only in Forest City; random police interviews
events.description: OSC MM2H notice: Platinum/Gold/Silver participants get one year after pass endorsement to buy their home; SEZ/SFZ participants must buy from Forest City (Johor) developers only, before endorsement, with sales reported to IMFC-J; fixed deposits encouraged in ringgit equivalent to the USD amounts; 50% withdrawal for homes bought up to two years (SEZ: six months) before endorsement; random interviews of prospective participants by the police (PDRM) in addition to security screening; housing information form; conditional approval letters.
events.quote: lokasi bagi tujuan pembelian rumah di bawah kategori Zon Khas Ekonomi/ Zon Khas Kewangan adalah di Forest City, Johor sahaja

ledger.contains: Written text of oral reply no. 22 (23 Oct 2019) by the Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture: describes MM2H (since 2002; 10-year renewable multiple-entry Social Visit Pass), 43,466 approvals from 131 countries 2002-Nov 2018, and a table of approvals for the top ten nationalities plus 'others' with a total of 43,943. The top-ten rows, both totals and the launch event were already in the data; the 'others' row (9,190) and the number of nationalities (131) are added. Parts add up to the table total 43,943 (not to the 43,466 in the text).

Written reply no. 159 (Oct-Dec 2019 sitting) by the Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture: 39,295 applications received 2011-Sept 2019, 31,185 approved 2011-July 2019 from 131 countries, and an estimated RM18.3 billion contribution to the economy over 17 years (visa fees, fixed deposits, home purchases). The three amounts were already in the data; the number of nationalities (131) is added. No table.

Written reply no. 256 (7 Dec 2020) by the Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture: 9,539 foreigners approved from 2018 to September 2019, a table of approvals for the top ten countries in 2018 and Jan-Sept 2019 (no total row, so no sum check; the ten rows give no 'others'), the freeze of the programme, and 5,396 applications returned to applicants through consultants. The question also asked for rejections and pending cases; the reply does not give them. Table rows, the 9,539 total and the freeze event were already in the data; the 5,396 returned applications are added.

Written text of oral reply no. 27 (4 Oct 2021, answered with no. 41) by the Home Minister on the revised MM2H: reactivation with applications handled by the Immigration Department from October 2021; nine new conditions (90 days' stay a year, offshore income RM40,000 a month instead of RM10,000, fixed deposit RM1 million with 50% withdrawal, age groups 35-49 and 50+ with RM50,000 extra deposit per dependant for the younger group, 5-year pass instead of 10, liquid assets RM1.5 million, pass fee RM500 a year instead of RM90, processing fee RM5,000 plus RM2,500 per dependant, security screening, good-conduct letter); policy changes (cap of 1% of Malaysian citizens, no low-skilled or security-sector applicants, monitoring, online system); 1-year conditional extension for existing participants; reasons, including the Auditor-General's report of 6 Oct 2020. Fixed deposit, income, liquid assets and fee terms and the announcement event were already in the data; stay, age, withdrawal, pass validity, cap and extension terms are added. The RM50,000 per dependant is already in the applies_to of the existing RM1 million fixed-deposit term.

PAC chair's media statement (16 Dec 2021) on tabling the PAC report on MM2H management: the Auditor-General's 2019 Series 2 report tabled 28 Sept 2021; hearings on 24 Nov, 1 Dec and 2 Dec 2021 and witnesses; eight findings (records not kept systematically, no full record of property values owned by participants, renewals after the first 10 years not verifiable, differing readings of Immigration Circular 6/2009 on children's age limit, no security threat from participants since 2002, new criteria not applied to existing participants except the RM500 fee, little stakeholder engagement); five recommendations. Both events were already in the data; the RM500 fee for existing participants is added as a term. No statistics.

PAC report DR.5/2022 (42 pp.): PAC follow-up report on the five recommendations of its MM2H report DR.24/2021, with ministry responses (pp. 1-10), and the transcript of the 16 March 2022 hearing (pp. 11-42). In scope: benchmarking and KPMG impact study; MOTAC projection of annual applications rising from 1,800 (2022) to 4,000 by 2025; 340 active licensed MM2H companies at 31 Dec 2021; Immigration takeover from 16 Sept 2021; NIISe system (go-live Dec 2023, full use Dec 2024, cost RM1.2 billion for the whole immigration system, not the programme); property purchase not compulsory and recorded only via fixed-deposit withdrawals; 211 applications under the new rules since September 2021; old fixed deposit RM150,000-350,000 and other old vs new conditions as spoken; 12 participants recorded buying homes worth RM16.7 million (16 Sept 2021-Feb 2022); 50% withdrawal limit; child dependants up to 34 under the 2022 Immigration amendment; predecessor programme from 1996; about 30 Tourism Malaysia offices abroad promoting MM2H (not a programme statistic). Previously recorded: 211 applications, the two projections, 12 buyers, the old fixed-deposit term. Added: 340 licensed agents, RM16.7 million property value, the child age term and three events. Spoken restatements of the new conditions (RM40,000 income, RM1 million deposit, RM500 fee, 90 days) are already terms from the 2021 parliamentary reply and are not duplicated.

One-page MOTAC table of the four MM2H categories (Platinum, Gold, Silver, SEZ/SFZ by age): fixed deposit, pass term, minimum age, compulsory home purchase price, participating fee, processing fee, minimum days in Malaysia by age, fixed-deposit withdrawal, dependants (children to 35 and single; parents and in-laws allowed), tax exemption on foreign income and fixed-deposit profit, renewal fee. Fixed-deposit, home, participating and renewal fee terms were already in the data from this table; processing fees, pass terms, minimum ages, stay, withdrawal and child-age terms are added. The SEZ home price is 'as set for SEZ property development' (no amount). The only image is a logo.

Two-page OSC MM2H (MOTAC) notice dated 28 May 2025 (the source row's published date is December 2025, the upload month): home-purchase deadline for Platinum/Gold/Silver, Forest City-only home purchase for SEZ/SFZ, ringgit fixed deposits encouraged, conditions for the 50% fixed-deposit withdrawal for homes bought before endorsement, random police interviews, housing form, conditional approval letters. No statistics. Three terms and one event added.

One-page MOTAC announcement: the MM2H information management system (mm2h.gov.my/portal) is used for new applications from 1 August 2025, processing fee RM500 (excluding SST) per application, helpdesk number. Images are the ministry logo and a screenshot of the login page (OCR checked, msa+eng: no other content). The fee term and the event were already in the data; nothing new.

mm2h.gov.my web page for the Silver category (last updated 10 Feb 2026): USD150,000 fixed deposit with 50% withdrawal, RM1,000 participating fee, compulsory home of RM600,000+ not to be sold for 10 years, 90 days' stay a year, dependants (spouse, children under 21 or 21-34 single and unemployed, disabled children, parents and in-laws), 5-year renewable pass, education, medical, no business or work, medical check-up, tax exemption, change of principal on death, renewal documents and RM1,500 renewal fee. Visitor counters on the page are not programme data. No terms were taken from this page before; nine terms added.
